==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|ev'ry||poetic}}
* {{alt|en|ivery||obsolete}}
* {{alt|en|euery||obsolete}}
* {{alt|en|e'ry||colloquial}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂ey-|id1=life|*perkʷ-|*kʷ-|*leyg-|id4=like}}
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:every|tree=1}}
{{inh+|en|enm|every,everich,everych}}, from {{inh|en|ang|[[ǣfre]] [[ǣlċ]],ǣfre [[ǣġhwelċ]]|each and every}}. {{surf|en|ever|each}} or {{com|en|ever|which}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɛv.(ə.)ɹi/|a=RP,GA,CA}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-every.ogg|a=US}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈev.(ə.)ɹi/|a=AU,NZ}}
* {{hyphenation|en|ev|ery}} 
* {{hyph|en|ev|e|ry|nocaption=1}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɛvɹi|s=2}}

===Determiner===
{{en-head|det}}

# {{cap|all}} of a countable group (considered individually), without exception.
#: {{ux|en|'''Every''' person in the room stood and cheered.}}
#: {{ux|en|She watches my '''every''' move.}}
#* {{RQ:Besant Ivory Gate|III
|passage=At half-past nine on this Saturday evening, the parlour of the Salutation Inn, High Holborn, contained most of its customary visitors.{{...}}In former days '''every''' tavern of repute kept such a room for its own select circle, a club, or society, of habitués, who met '''every''' evening, for a pipe and a cheerful glass.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=5|passage=Here, in the transept and choir, where the service was being held, one was conscious '''every''' moment of an increasing brightness; colours glowing vividly beneath the circular chandeliers, and the rows of small lights on the choristers' desks flashed and sparkled in front of the boys' faces, deep linen collars, and red neckbands.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-06-07|author=David Simpson
|volume=188|issue=26|page=36|magazine=w:The Guardian Weekly
|title=[http://www.guardian.co.uk/books/2013/may/18/falling-upwards-richard-holmes-review Fantasy of navigation]
|passage=Like most human activities, ballooning has sponsored heroes and hucksters and a good deal in between. For '''every''' dedicated scientist patiently recording atmospheric pressure and wind speed while shivering at high altitudes, there is a carnival barker with a bevy of pretty girls willing to dangle from a basket or parachute down to earth.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2022|author=[[w:Kelly Yang|Kelly Yang]]|title=New From Here|page=272
|passage=There's fire in his '''every''' step as he stares straight ahead.}}
# {{n-g|Denotes equal spacing at a stated interval, or a proportion corresponding to such a spacing.}}
#: {{ux|en|We stopped for refreshments '''every''' ten miles.}}
#: {{ux|en|The alarm is going off '''every''' few minutes.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Every''' third bead was red, and the rest were blue. The sequence was thus red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue etc.}}
#: {{ux|en|Decimation originally meant the execution of '''every''' tenth soldier in a unit; that is, ten per cent of soldiers were killed.}}
# {{lb|en|[[with]] [[certain]] [[noun]]s}} {{n-g|Denotes an abundance of something.}}
#: {{ux|en|We wish you '''every''' happiness in the future.}}
#: {{ux|en|He shows '''every''' sign of becoming an excellent player. I have '''every''' confidence in him.}}
#: {{ux|en|There is '''every''' reason why we shouldn't.}}
#: {{ux|en|The police will make '''every''' effort to trace the missing girl.}}

====Usage notes====
* Now generally used only for a group of three or more, but formerly could be used for two, in the sense of "each" or "both":

:* {{quote-book|en|year=1828|author=James Hogg|title=Mary Burnet
|passage=But it is true that I tell ye; our dear bairn is to meet us at Moffat the morn, wi' a son in '''every''' hand; and we maun e'en gang and see her aince again, and kiss her and bless her afore we dee.}}

* {{l|en|no}}
